entries.text: .duckdb.err[handle] The reason behind the last 'duckdb signal, first line the cause, cleared by the next call. err[] is any connection's, err[handle] that connection's. Return: string Examples @[.duckdb.exec[.duckdb.main[]];"SELECT * FROM no_such_table";{.duckdb.err[]}] Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.exec
entries.title: .duckdb.exec[handle;sql]
entries.text: .duckdb.exec[handle;sql] Run SQL on a handle and answer the result as a table; a statement without a result answers ::. Examples .duckdb.exec[.duckdb.main[];"SELECT 1 AS one, 'a' AS s"] Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.hdel
entries.title: .duckdb.hdel[handle;table]
entries.text: .duckdb.hdel[handle;table] Drop a table (or view) of the handle's catalog. hdel `:pq:duckdb:alias:table/ is the same verb. A q global bound to it stays bound and errors on use. Return: table Examples .duckdb.exec[.duckdb.main[];"CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE u AS SELECT 1 AS a"] .duckdb.hdel[.duckdb.main[];`u] Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.load
entries.title: .duckdb.load[handle;names]
entries.text: .duckdb.load[handle;names] Bind the handle's tables and views as q globals at the root, later-wins. \l `:pq:duckdb:alias is the same door. Return: the names bound Parameters: names - () for none, :: for all, else the table names Examples .duckdb.load[.duckdb.main[];::] Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.main
entries.title: .duckdb.main[]
entries.text: .duckdb.main[] The handle of the process's own DuckDB database, `:pq:duckdb:main: in-memory, or the file q -duckdb path names. Opened on the first call; every alias is a catalog attached to it, and .parquet and s) run here. Return: `:pq:duckdb:main Examples .duckdb.exec[.duckdb.main[];"SELECT current_database()"] Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.onsql
entries.title: .duckdb.onsql[row]
entries.text: .duckdb.onsql[row] Called once per statement with its log row as a dict. Rebind it to route the log elsewhere, or set it to (::) for none. Do not close the connection or issue transaction control from a handler: it runs mid-statement. Examples .duckdb.onsql:{[row] -1 row`sql;} Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.secret
entries.title: .duckdb.secret[name;typ;opts]
entries.text: .duckdb.secret[name;typ;opts] Create or replace a DuckDB secret (the credentials httpfs uses for s3:// gcs:// hf://), or drop one. opts ride verbatim as KEY value clauses of CREATE SECRET, so an unknown key is DuckDB's own refusal; the key `persistent (boolean) picks the persistent form, which outlives the process in DuckDB's own store. Return: name Paramete

entries.name: .duckdb.secrets
entries.title: .duckdb.secrets[]
entries.text: .duckdb.secrets[] The secrets defined, without their values. col: scope the URL prefixes the secret covers Examples .duckdb.secrets[] Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.sqllog
entries.title: .duckdb.sqllog
entries.text: .duckdb.sqllog The statement log: one row per statement the bridge issued, newest last. Examples select time, dur, sql from .duckdb.sqllog Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.types
entries.title: .duckdb.types[]
entries.text: .duckdb.types[] The DuckDB-to-q type map as a table, one row per contract entry. Columns: needs - what a schema row must carry to round-trip: none, logical, dtype or both dtype - the DuckDB DDL spelling logical - the logical type name ktype - the .duckdb.meta type char canon - whether a bare read of that DuckDB type produces this row Examples select from .du

entries.name: .duckdb.unsafeExecText
entries.title: .duckdb.unsafeExecText[handle;sql]
entries.text: .duckdb.unsafeExecText[handle;sql] Run any statement and answer DuckDB's own rendering as text, bypassing the type map: rows as DuckDB prints them, or the error message as data when the statement fails. A diagnostic, not a query door. Return: string Examples .duckdb.unsafeExecText[.duckdb.main[];"SELECT [1,2,3] AS arr, {'a': 1} AS st"] Copy

entries.name: .duckdb.unsafeText
entries.title: .duckdb.unsafeText[handle;tableName]
entries.text: .duckdb.unsafeText[handle;tableName] A table as DuckDB renders it, every column cast to VARCHAR (so nested, UUID, ENUM and BIT cells show), NULL as the text NULL, rows in insertion order. A text cell holding a newline or " | " misaligns its row. Return: a table of one string column per column of tableName Examples .duckdb.exec[.duckdb.main[];"CREATE OR REPLA

entries.name: .ffi.bind
entries.title: .ffi.bind[funcname;argtypes;returntype]
entries.text: .ffi.bind[funcname;argtypes;returntype] Resolve a C function once and answer a q function that calls it. The result is unary: it takes ONE list of arguments ending in (::) - the trailing :: stops q collapsing same-type arguments into a vector. Parameters: funcname - `fn resolvable in this process, or `lib`fn to load a library argtypes - one type letter per a

entries.name: .ffi.callFunction
entries.title: .ffi.callFunction[returnfunc;arglist]
entries.text: .ffi.callFunction[returnfunc;arglist] Call a C function, resolving it every time, with argument types inferred from the values. Parameters: arglist - the arguments, ending in (::) returnfunc - `fn, `lib`fn, or (returnletter;fn) - the letter defaults to "i" Examples .ffi.callFunction[("f";`libm.so.6`sqrt)] (16f;::) Copy

entries.name: .ffi.cvar
entries.title: .ffi.cvar[returnvar]
entries.text: .ffi.cvar[returnvar] Read a C global variable. Parameters: returnvar - `var, `lib`var, or (typeletter;var)

entries.name: .ffi.extension
entries.title: .ffi.extension[]
entries.text: .ffi.extension[] This platform's shared-library extension. Return: `so, `dll or `dylib Examples ` sv `libmylib,.ffi.extension[] Copy

entries.name: .ffi.os
entries.title: .ffi.os[]
entries.text: .ffi.os[] This platform's OS letter, as ffikdb examples branch on it. Return: "l", "w" or "m" Examples "l"=.ffi.os[] Copy

entries.name: .ffi.ptrsize
entries.title: .ffi.ptrsize[]
entries.text: .ffi.ptrsize[] The width of a pointer on this platform, in bytes. Return: 8i, or 4i on a 32-bit host

entries.name: .ffi.setErrno
entries.title: .ffi.setErrno[errnum]
entries.text: .ffi.setErrno[errnum] Set errno and answer its previous value; anything but an int atom reads without setting. Return: the previous errno Examples .ffi.setErrno[] Copy

entries.name: .massive.bars
entries.title: .massive.bars[ticker;start;end;opts]
entries.text: .massive.bars[ticker;start;end;opts] Bars for a ticker between two dates. Parameters: opts - `span (`day `hour `minute) and `mult set the bar size: `mult`span!(5;`minute) is 5-minute bars Examples .massive.bars[`AAPL;2026.08.01;2026.09.05;()!()] Copy .massive.bars[`AAPL;2026.09.05;2026.09.05;`mult`span!(5;`minute)] Copy

entries.name: .massive.daily
entries.title: .massive.daily[date;adjusted;opts]
entries.text: .massive.daily[date;adjusted;opts] Every US stock's daily bar for one date. Parameters: adjusted - 1b for split-adjusted prices Examples .massive.daily[2026.09.05;1b;()!()] Copy

entries.name: .massive.divs
entries.title: .massive.divs[opts]
entries.text: .massive.divs[opts] Dividends. Parameters: opts - API filters such as `ticker`ex_dividend_date Examples .massive.divs[(enlist `ticker)!enlist `AAPL] Copy

entries.name: .massive.fetch
entries.title: .massive.fetch[request]
entries.text: .massive.fetch[request] GET any API path and answer its payload as a table (one page, no paging). Parameters: request - a path string, or (path;params dict) Examples .massive.fetch ("/v3/reference/tickers";(enlist `limit)!enlist 5) Copy

entries.name: .massive.ipos
entries.title: .massive.ipos[opts]
entries.text: .massive.ipos[opts] IPOs. Parameters: opts - API filters such as `ticker`listing_date

entries.name: .massive.news
entries.title: .massive.news[opts]
entries.text: .massive.news[opts] News articles. Parameters: opts - API filters such as `ticker`published_utc Examples .massive.news[`ticker`max!(`AAPL;20)] Copy

entries.name: .massive.ohlc
entries.title: .massive.ohlc[ticker;date;opts]
entries.text: .massive.ohlc[ticker;date;opts] One ticker's open, high, low and close for one date. Examples .massive.ohlc[`AAPL;2026.09.05;()!()] Copy

entries.name: .massive.prevclose
entries.title: .massive.prevclose[ticker;opts]
entries.text: .massive.prevclose[ticker;opts] The previous day's open, high, low, close and volume for a ticker. Examples .massive.prevclose[`AAPL;()!()] Copy

entries.name: .massive.quotes
entries.title: .massive.quotes[ticker;opts]
entries.text: .massive.quotes[ticker;opts] Tick-level quotes for a ticker. Parameters: opts - API filters such as `timestamp`limit bound the range Examples .massive.quotes[`AAPL;`timestamp`limit!(2026.09.05;100)] Copy

entries.name: .massive.snap
entries.title: .massive.snap[tickers;opts]
entries.text: .massive.snap[tickers;opts] The current snapshot (last trade, last quote, today's bar) for a list of tickers. Examples .massive.snap[`AAPL`MSFT;()!()] Copy

entries.name: .massive.splits
entries.title: .massive.splits[opts]
entries.text: .massive.splits[opts] Stock splits. Parameters: opts - API filters such as `ticker`execution_date Examples .massive.splits[(enlist `ticker)!enlist `AAPL] Copy

entries.name: .massive.status
entries.title: .massive.status[]
entries.text: .massive.status[] Whether the market is open now: the exchanges, their state and the server time. Examples .massive.status[] Copy

entries.name: .massive.tickers
entries.title: .massive.tickers[opts]
entries.text: .massive.tickers[opts] The reference list of tickers. Parameters: opts - API filters such as `market`exchange`search`active Examples .massive.tickers[`search`active!("apple";1b)] Copy

entries.name: .massive.trades
entries.title: .massive.trades[ticker;opts]
entries.text: .massive.trades[ticker;opts] Tick-level trades for a ticker. Parameters: opts - API filters such as `timestamp`limit bound the range Examples .massive.trades[`AAPL;`timestamp`limit!(2026.09.05;100)] Copy

entries.name: .parquet.bloom_probe
entries.title: .parquet.bloom_probe[file;column;val]
entries.text: .parquet.bloom_probe[file;column;val] Per row group, whether the bloom filter on a column excludes a value: DuckDB's parquet_bloom_probe. Examples .parquet.bloom_probe[`:t.parquet;`a;1] Copy

entries.name: .parquet.file_metadata
entries.title: .parquet.file_metadata[file]
entries.text: .parquet.file_metadata[file] The file-level metadata: created_by, num_rows, num_row_groups, format_version, encryption_algorithm. Examples .parquet.file_metadata `:t.parquet Copy

entries.name: .parquet.kv_metadata
entries.title: .parquet.kv_metadata[file]
entries.text: .parquet.kv_metadata[file] The file's key-value metadata, one row per key (a q-written file carries q_schema). Examples .parquet.kv_metadata `:t.parquet Copy

entries.name: .parquet.metadata
entries.title: .parquet.metadata[file]
entries.text: .parquet.metadata[file] One row per column chunk per row group: DuckDB's parquet_metadata. Examples select path_in_schema, row_group_id, num_values from .parquet.metadata `:t.parquet Copy

entries.name: .parquet.schema
entries.title: .parquet.schema[file]
entries.text: .parquet.schema[file] The file's schema: one row per column, DuckDB's parquet_schema columns verbatim. Examples .parquet.schema `:t.parquet Copy

entries.name: .pq.cancolor
entries.title: .pq.cancolor[x]
entries.text: .pq.cancolor[x] Whether stdout should carry ANSI colour: PEACHQ_COLORS=0/1 overrides everything, then NO_COLOR (off), FORCE_COLOR (on), else a tty whose TERM is not dumb. Return: boolean Examples .pq.cancolor[] Copy

entries.name: .pq.conns
entries.title: .pq.conns[]
entries.text: .pq.conns[] Every open connection, one row each. The single-letter columns p f z n m are the -38! names so kdb code ports. Columns: alias - the :pq: alias, when the connection opened with one handle - what hclose takes: the alias symbol of a :pq: provider, else the fd int Examples .pq.conns[] Copy

entries.name: .pq.dr
entries.title: .pq.dr[verb]
entries.text: .pq.dr[verb] Print a verb's domain and range grid in the layout the KX reference pages use, probed by casting a sample of every type: a lower-case letter is an atom result, upper-case a list, "." an error. Parameters: verb - a symbol or char naming a verb in .Q.ops[], or a function Examples .pq.dr `neg Copy .pq.dr "+" Copy

entries.name: .pq.termsize
entries.title: .pq.termsize[x]
entries.text: .pq.termsize[x] The live terminal size, with the 25/80 fallback and [10,2000] clamp that \c 0N uses. Return: (rows;cols) Examples .pq.termsize[] Copy

entries.name: .regexp.duckdb_match
entries.title: .regexp.duckdb_match[handle]
entries.text: .regexp.duckdb_match[handle] Whether an open DuckDB handle's RE2 is the version vendored here; answers a boolean rather than signalling, since PEACHQ_DUCKDB_LIB may legitimately point at another release. Examples .regexp.duckdb_match .duckdb.main[] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.escape
entries.title: .regexp.escape[text]
entries.text: .regexp.escape[text] The pattern that matches text literally (RE2's QuoteMeta). Examples .regexp.matches["1+1=2";.regexp.escape "1+1"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.extract
entries.title: .regexp.extract[subject;pattern]
entries.text: .regexp.extract[subject;pattern] The first matched text, "" when nothing matches. Examples .regexp.extract["abc123";"[0-9]+"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.extract_all
entries.title: .regexp.extract_all[subject;pattern]
entries.text: .regexp.extract_all[subject;pattern] Every non-overlapping match. Examples .regexp.extract_all["a1b22c333";"[0-9]+"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.full_match
entries.title: .regexp.full_match[subject;pattern]
entries.text: .regexp.full_match[subject;pattern] Does the pattern match the whole subject? Examples .regexp.full_match["abc";"a.c"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.groups
entries.title: .regexp.groups[subject;pattern]
entries.text: .regexp.groups[subject;pattern] The capture groups of the first match, () when nothing matches. Examples .regexp.groups["2026-09-19";"(\\d+)-(\\d+)-(\\d+)"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.groups_all
entries.title: .regexp.groups_all[subject;pattern]
entries.text: .regexp.groups_all[subject;pattern] One group list per match, so .regexp.groups_all[...][;1] is the second group across every match. Examples .regexp.groups_all["a=1, b=2";"(\\w)=(\\d)"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.matches
entries.title: .regexp.matches[subject;pattern]
entries.text: .regexp.matches[subject;pattern] Does the pattern match anywhere in the subject? Examples .regexp.matches["Hello";"(?i)^h"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.replace
entries.title: .regexp.replace[subject;pattern;replacement]
entries.text: .regexp.replace[subject;pattern;replacement] The first match replaced. Parameters: replacement - may name capture groups as \1 to \9 Examples .regexp.replace["2026-09-19";"(\\d+)-(\\d+)-(\\d+)";"\\3/\\2/\\1"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.replace_all
entries.title: .regexp.replace_all[subject;pattern;replacement]
entries.text: .regexp.replace_all[subject;pattern;replacement] Every match replaced. Parameters: replacement - may name capture groups as \1 to \9 Examples .regexp.replace_all["a1b2";"[0-9]";"#"] ↗

entries.name: .regexp.split
entries.title: .regexp.split[subject;pattern]
entries.text: .regexp.split[subject;pattern] The subject split on the pattern; no match answers the subject itself as one piece. Examples .regexp.split["a, b;c";"[,;] *"] ↗

entries.name: .str.format
entries.title: .str.format[msg]
entries.text: .str.format[msg] Python-style formatting (DuckDB's format grammar): {} {0} {:>8.2f} {:,}; a plain string only has {{ }} unescaped. Parameters: msg - a format string, or a list of one plus its arguments Examples .str.format ("{:>6}|{:,}";"ab";1234567) Copy

entries.name: .str.isalnum
entries.title: .str.isalnum[text]
entries.text: .str.isalnum[text] Is every character a letter or a digit, and is there at least one? "_" is neither.

entries.name: .str.islower
entries.title: .str.islower[text]
entries.text: .str.islower[text] Is every cased character lower case, and is there at least one? "abc1" is 1b.

entries.name: .str.isupper
entries.title: .str.isupper[text]
entries.text: .str.isupper[text] Is every cased character upper case, and is there at least one? "ABC1" is 1b.

entries.name: .str.printf
entries.title: .str.printf[msg]
entries.text: .str.printf[msg] C-style formatting (DuckDB's printf grammar): %d %s %.2f %'d groups thousands, %,d spells the comma; %r renders any q value; a plain string only has %% unescaped. Parameters: msg - a format string, or a list of one plus its arguments Examples .str.printf ("%s: %'d rows in %.1fs";"trade";1234567;0.25) Copy

entries.name: .str.removeprefix
entries.title: .str.removeprefix[text;prefix]
entries.text: .str.removeprefix[text;prefix] text without one leading prefix, unchanged when it does not start with it. Examples .str.removeprefix["v1.2";"v"] Copy

entries.name: .str.startswith
entries.title: .str.startswith[text;prefix]
entries.text: .str.startswith[text;prefix] Does text begin with prefix? An empty prefix always does. Examples .str.startswith[("apple";"banana");"a"] Copy

entries.name: .termbox.beep
entries.title: .termbox.beep[hz;ms]
entries.text: .termbox.beep[hz;ms] Start a tone of hz for ms milliseconds and return at once (one plays at a time): 1b when a tone was started, 0b when one is still playing (the call is dropped) or there was no audio device and the terminal bell rang instead. Parameters: hz - 0-32767; 0 is silence ms - 0-60000 Examples .termbox.beep[440;200] Copy

entries.name: .termbox.cells
entries.title: .termbox.cells[]
entries.text: .termbox.cells[] The back buffer as a table with one row per cell, ch a long codepoint: what present would send, before it is sent. col: ch the codepoint; "c"$ it for ASCII text Examples select from .termbox.cells[] where ch < >32 Copy

entries.name: .termbox.clear
entries.title: .termbox.clear[]
entries.text: .termbox.clear[] Blank every cell of the back buffer (space, default colours). Nothing shows until present.

entries.name: .termbox.events
entries.title: .termbox.events[ms]
entries.text: .termbox.events[ms] Every pending event as a table with peek_event's columns, one row per event in arrival order: waits at most ms milliseconds for the first, then takes what is already queued. Empty when nothing arrived. Parameters: ms - the timeout for the first event; negative waits forever Examples select name, ch from .termbox.events 100 Copy

entries.name: .termbox.init
entries.title: .termbox.init[]
entries.text: .termbox.init[] Take the terminal: raw input, the alternate screen, cursor hidden. throws: os - stdin/stdout is not a terminal domain - a session is already open

entries.name: .termbox.peek_event
entries.title: .termbox.peek_event[ms]
entries.text: .termbox.peek_event[ms] Wait up to ms milliseconds for an event and answer it as a dict; a field that does not apply is null. Mouse events arrive only after set_input_mode with .termbox.input.mouse. There are no key-release events. Columns: button - `left`right`middle`wheel_up`wheel_down`release, `none for a plain movement mod - the sum of 1 shift, 2 alt, 4

entries.name: .termbox.poll_event
entries.title: .termbox.poll_event[]
entries.text: .termbox.poll_event[] Wait for the next event, with no timeout. peek_event's answer.

entries.name: .termbox.present
entries.title: .termbox.present[]
entries.text: .termbox.present[] Write the back buffer to the terminal: only the cells that changed since the last present are sent. A resized window is noticed here; the next peek_event answers a `resize event.

entries.name: .termbox.print
entries.title: .termbox.print
entries.text: .termbox.print Write a string into the back buffer from column x, row y, one cell per character (a multibyte UTF-8 character is one cell); text past the right edge is dropped. .termbox.print[x;y;fg;bg;text;w;align] places the text inside a w-cell field starting at x, aligned `left, `centre (`center) or `right, clipped to the field. Parameters: fg - a style,

entries.name: .termbox.rgb
entries.title: .termbox.rgb[r;g;b]
entries.text: .termbox.rgb[r;g;b] A 24-bit colour as a style long. Styles are disjoint bit fields, so add colours and attributes. Parameters: r - 0-255 b - 0-255 g - 0-255 Examples .termbox.rgb[255;128;0]+.termbox.attribute.bold Copy

entries.name: .termbox.set_cell
entries.title: .termbox.set_cell[x;y;ch;fg;bg]
entries.text: .termbox.set_cell[x;y;ch;fg;bg] Write one cell of the back buffer at column x, row y (0-based). A position off the screen is ignored. Parameters: fg - a style: .termbox.color. or .termbox.rgb[r;g;b], plus any .termbox.attribute. ch - a char, or a Unicode codepoint as a long Examples .termbox.set_cell[0;0;"@";.termbox.color.red+.termbox.attribute.bold;.termbo

entries.name: .termbox.set_cells
entries.title: .termbox.set_cells[x;y;ch;fg;bg]
entries.text: .termbox.set_cells[x;y;ch;fg;bg] Write many cells at once: cell i lands at x[i], y[i]. Cells off the screen are dropped. Parameters: fg - a style for every cell, or a long vector with one per cell ch - one char or codepoint for every cell, a string with one byte per cell, a long vector of codepoints, or a list of strings each decoding from UTF-8 to one codep

entries.name: .termbox.set_cursor
entries.title: .termbox.set_cursor[x;y]
entries.text: .termbox.set_cursor[x;y] Place the cursor at column x, row y (0-based; shown at the next present). A negative coordinate hides it.

entries.name: .termbox.set_input_mode
entries.title: .termbox.set_input_mode[mode]
entries.text: .termbox.set_input_mode[mode] Choose how input is read: a sum of .termbox.input. values. .termbox.input.mouse turns mouse reporting on (clicks, wheel, releases and every pointer movement); esc and alt both read Esc-prefixed keys as alt-modified. Return: the previous mode Examples .termbox.set_input_mode .termbox.input.esc+.termbox.input.mouse Copy

entries.name: .termbox.set_output_mode
entries.title: .termbox.set_output_mode[mode]
entries.text: .termbox.set_output_mode[mode] Choose how colours are sent: a .termbox.output. value. init picks the richest the terminal reports (COLORTERM, TERM); NO_COLOR or PEACHQ_COLORS=0 picks mono. A style richer than the mode degrades to the nearest colour the mode has. Return: the previous mode Examples .termbox.set_output_mode .termbox.output.color256 Copy

entries.name: .termbox.show
entries.title: .termbox.show
entries.text: .termbox.show Paint whole rows from the top-left corner, row y from the string at y. .termbox.show[rows;fg;bg] also styles them: a style atom for everything, a long vector with one style per row, or a list of long vectors with one style per cell. Rows below the screen and cells past the right edge are dropped. Examples .termbox.show ("row 0";"row 1") Copy .t

entries.name: .termbox.shutdown
entries.title: .termbox.shutdown[]
entries.text: .termbox.shutdown[] Hand the terminal back exactly as init found it. Safe to call when no session is open.

entries.name: .termbox.wrap
entries.title: .termbox.wrap[width;text]
entries.text: .termbox.wrap[width;text] Word-wrap text to width cells (a multibyte character is one cell): breaks at spaces, a newline starts a new line, a word wider than the width is split where it must be. Needs no session. Return: a list of strings Examples .termbox.wrap[10;"the quick brown fox jumps"] Copy
